diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us importantly {point out} that, from the Aronson type inequality \eqref{ineq-density-scheme} for the scheme, it readily follows that ${g_{s,x}^{h,\varepsilon}(t)}\lesssim h^{-\frac{\gamma_\varepsilon}\alpha}<+\infty $. In particular, this means that this quantity can be used in a Gronwall or circular type procedure as we actually do below.
Equation \eqref{holder-space-gammah} then follows taking the supremum in time in the previous inequality provided $T $ is small enough.

issues.failure_explanation: For \alpha=2 the denominator of g_{s,x}^{h,\varepsilon} uses the exact Gaussian density p_2 of the noise, but the Aronson bound \eqref{ineq-density-scheme} controls \Gamma^h only by the proxy \bar p_2, whose variance constant must be strictly larger than that of p_2 (already for one Euler step, \E[p_2(h,y-x-b(U,x)h)]/p_2(h,y-x) is unbounded in y-x, so c=1 is impossible). Hence \bar p_2/p_2 is unbounded and the claimed finiteness fails: for constant drift b\equiv B\neq0, \Gamma^h(0,x,t,y)=p_2(t,y-x-Bt) exactly, and the defining supremum is +\infty (take z'=x, z=x+\lambda B, \lambda\to\infty). The inference 'from \eqref{ineq-density-scheme} it readily follows that g\lesssim h^{-\gamma_\varepsilon/\alpha}<+\infty' is therefore false for \alpha=2, and the circular absorption argument that closes the proof of \eqref{holder-space-gammah} is invalid in the Brownian case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define g_{s,x}^{h,\varepsilon} with \bar p_\alpha instead of p_\alpha in the denominator (as done for the diffusion's h^{\varepsilon,\eta} and consistently with the later displays of the same proof). Then \eqref{ineq-density-scheme} yields g\lesssim h^{-\gamma_\varepsilon/\alpha}<\infty, and the rest of the proof is unchanged; for \alpha\in(1,2) the two definitions are equivalent by \eqref{EQ_PALPHA_BARPALPHA_JUMPS}.
issues.overall_effect: For \alpha=2 the bootstrap quantity can be infinite, so the self-consistent closing argument for the scheme's forward spatial Hölder estimate \eqref{holder-space-gammah} does not run; the Brownian case of Lemma THE_LEMMA_FOR_THM and of Theorem thm-main, which rely on \eqref{holder-space-gammah}, lose their proof.
issues.title: Bootstrap quantity for the scheme Hölder estimate is infinite in the Gaussian case
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single forced change of denominator that makes the finiteness claim and the whole closing argument valid, with no change to any statement, method, rate, or regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The recursive bound for g_{0,x}^{h,\varepsilon}(t) is derived only in the regime |y-y'|^\alpha\vee h\le t (used explicitly in the last inequality of the gathering) and uses (\tau_s^h)^{-\beta/\alpha}\lesssim t^{-\beta/\alpha}, which requires \tau_s^h\gtrsim t, i.e. t\gtrsim h (for s\ge t/2, \tau_s^h\ge t/2-h, which can be 0 when t\lesssim h). But g is defined as a supremum over all (z,z')\in(\R^d)^2 and the closing argument takes a supremum over all t\in(0,T]; the complementary regimes (|y-y'|^\alpha\vee h>t, and t\lesssim h) are never treated, so the absorption 'provided T is small enough' does not bound the full supremum as written.

failure_location.quote: using as well that  $ |y'-y|^\alpha\vee h \le t $ for the last inequality. Since $ \gamma-\beta=\alpha-1>0$, Equation \eqref{holder-space-gammah} then follows taking the supremum in time in the previous inequality provided $T $ is small enough.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the complementary cases: if |y-y'|^\alpha\vee h>t, the ratio defining g is \le C directly from the Aronson bound \eqref{ineq-density-scheme} (t^{\gamma_\varepsilon/\alpha}/(|z-z'|+h^{1/\alpha})^{\gamma_\varepsilon}\le 1); if t\le 4h, the target estimate \eqref{holder-space-gammah} follows from \eqref{ineq-density-scheme} since ((|y-y'|+h^{1/\alpha})/t^{1/\alpha})^{\gamma_\varepsilon}\ge 4^{-\gamma_\varepsilon/\alpha}. With these two lines the closing supremum argument goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The self-consistent inequality that is supposed to yield the uniform boundedness of g, and hence the scheme estimate \eqref{holder-space-gammah}, is established only on a restricted parameter range; the proof is formally incomplete on the complementary (off-diagonal and small-time) regimes, which are needed for the supremum.
issues.title: Scheme Hölder recursion closed only in restricted regimes; complementary cases untreated
issues.why_classification: Only degenerate-case bookkeeping is missing; the bypass is a short, standard Aronson-based estimate, and the method, statement, rate, and scope of \eqref{holder-space-gammah} all survive.

issues.failure_explanation: In the bounds for H_{32} and H_{33} the proof asserts \bar p_\alpha(s,y-x)\lesssim\bar p_\alpha(t,y-x) on intervals where s can be as small as (2t-t')/2. Under the hypothesis |t-t'|\le t-s of \eqref{holder-time-gamma} (with s=0 this allows t' up to 2t), when t' approaches 2t the claim is false near the diagonal: for y=x, \bar p_\alpha(s,0)/\bar p_\alpha(t,0)=(t/s)^{d/\alpha}, which is unbounded as t'/t\to2. Moreover, with the correct factor \bar p_\alpha(s,y-x), the off-diagonal (triangle-inequality) part of \eqref{pivot-post-cancel-2} produces, when d+\beta>\alpha, contributions exceeding the claimed (t'-t)^{\gamma/\alpha}(1+t^{-\beta/\alpha})\bar p_\alpha(t,y-x) by a factor (t/(2t-t'))^{(d+\beta-\alpha)/\alpha}. Hence \eqref{maj-H32-holder-time-gamma} and \eqref{maj-H33-holder-time-gamma} are not established in the regime t'-t\gtrsim t, and no alternative argument is supplied there.

failure_location.quote: along with the fact that for on the considered time interval, we have $t-s+\lambda (t'-t)\asymp t-s$ and  $ \bar{p}_\alpha (s,y-x)\lesssim \bar{p}_\alpha (t,y-x)$, we get

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the Duhamel analysis to t'-t\le t/2 (then s\ge t/4 on all sub-intervals and every comparability used is valid), and treat t'-t\ge t/2 directly from the Aronson bound \eqref{ineq-density-diff}: |\Gamma(0,x,t,y)-\Gamma(0,x,t',y)|\le C(\bar p_\alpha(t,y-x)+\bar p_\alpha(t',y-x))\lesssim((t'-t)/t)^{\gamma/\alpha}\bar p_\alpha(t',y-x) since ((t'-t)/t)^{\gamma/\alpha}\ge 2^{-\gamma/\alpha}.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the forward time-Hölder estimate \eqref{holder-time-gamma} is invalid in the regime t'-t\gtrsim t (allowed by its own hypothesis); since Theorem thm-main applies \eqref{holder-time-gamma} with s-\tau_s^h up to \tau_s^h (the full ratio range up to 2) in the \Delta_2 estimate, the main theorem's proof inherits the gap.
issues.title: Time-Hölder proof uses false comparability \bar p_\alpha(s,\cdot)\lesssim\bar p_\alpha(t,\cdot) for s\ll t; regime t'-t\approx t not treated
issues.why_classification: The repair is a regime restriction plus a two-line Aronson estimate for the complementary case; the statement of \eqref{holder-time-gamma} and all its applications survive with no loss of content or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assuming w.l.o.g. that $t> h$, then using \eqref{ineq-density-scheme}, \eqref{ineq-density-diff},

issues.failure_explanation: The decomposition \eqref{DECOUP_ERR} writes the density error as integrals over [0,h] (\Delta_1), [h,\tau_t^h-h] (\Delta_2-\Delta_5) and [\tau_t^h-h,t] (\Delta_6). This partitions [0,t] only when \tau_t^h-h\ge h; for t<2h one has \tau_t^h\le h, so the middle range is empty or inverted while [\tau_t^h-h,t]\supset[0,h] double-counts the range of \Delta_1, making the identity false. The theorem is stated for all t\in(0,T]. The phrase 'Assuming w.l.o.g. that t>h' only addresses the estimate of \Delta_1, and the later sub-splits at t/2 inside \Delta_4 degenerate as well for t\lesssim h; no small-time case is treated anywhere.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For t\le 4h, estimate the Duhamel difference directly without any decomposition: each of the two terms contributes \lesssim \|b\|_\infty\int_0^t(t-s)^{-1/\alpha}ds\,\bar p_\alpha(t,y-x)\lesssim t^{(\alpha-1)/\alpha}\bar p_\alpha(t,y-x), and t^{(\alpha-1)/\alpha}\le(4h)^{(\alpha-1)/\alpha}\lesssim h^{\gamma/\alpha}t^{-\beta/\alpha} since t\le 4h, matching \eqref{BD_THM}. The Grönwall recursion then runs for t>4h with the small-time values already controlled.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of Theorem thm-main covers only t\gtrsim h (at least t\ge 2h for the decomposition, and t\gtrsim h with margin for the t/2 sub-splits and the \tau_s^h\gtrsim t comparisons); the bound \eqref{BD_THM} for 0<t\lesssim h is unproven.
issues.title: Error decomposition \eqref{DECOUP_ERR} is an identity only for t\ge 2h; case t\lesssim h missing
issues.why_classification: The missing case is a degenerate small-time regime handled by a short direct estimate using only the Aronson bounds and the kernel gradient bound; the method, rate, and advertised scope of the theorem are all preserved.

issues.failure_explanation:
The scheme contribution to \Delta_6 in \eqref{DECOUP_ERR} is \E_{0,x}[b(U_{	au_s^h/h},X_{	au_s^h}^h)\cdot
abla_y p_\alpha(t-s,y-X_s^h)], where by \eqref{scheme-interpo} X_s^h=X_{	au_s^h}^h+b(U_{	au_s^h/h},X_{	au_s^h}^h)(s-	au_s^h)+Z_s-Z_{	au_s^h}. The displayed \Delta_{62} equals instead \E[b(U_{	au_s^h/h},X_{	au_s^h}^h)\cdot
abla_y p_\alpha(t-s,y-X_{	au_s^h}^h)]: it expands only through the density \Gamma^h(0,x,	au_s^h,\cdot) with the kernel evaluated at z and time t-s. The two are not equal: conditioning on \sigma(X_{	au_s^h}^h,U_{	au_s^h/h}) and using harmonicity of the stable kernel (the step used for \Delta_4) turns the kernel into 
abla_y p_\alpha(t-	au_s^h,y-X_{	au_s^h}^h-b(U_{	au_s^h/h},X_{	au_s^h}^h)(s-	au_s^h)), with a different time argument and an additional drift shift. That step is missing, so the bound \eqref{maj-D6-mainthm} is not justified as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the conditioning/harmonicity reduction used for \Delta_4: condition on \sigma(X_{\tau_s^h}^h,U_{\tau_s^h/h}), integrate the noise increment to get the kernel at time t-\tau_s^h with shift b(r,z)(s-\tau_s^h). The shift is diagonal (\|b\|_\infty(s-\tau_s^h)\lesssim(t-\tau_s^h)^{1/\alpha}), and t-\tau_s^h\ge t-s only improves the kernels, so the cancellation estimates yield exactly \eqref{maj-D6-mainthm}.
issues.overall_effect: The treatment of the last-time-step contribution \Delta_6 (hence the gathering estimate leading to the Grönwall argument, hence Theorem thm-main) rests on an incorrect identity for the scheme part.
issues.title: \Delta_{62} identity omits the conditioning/harmonicity step for the scheme term
issues.why_classification: The repair inserts a step that is already used identically elsewhere in the same proof, and the final estimate is unchanged; no statement, rate, or regime is lost.

issues.failure_explanation:
The decomposition \eqref{DECOUP_ERR} leaves \Delta_3=\int_h^{	au_t^h-h}\E[b(s,X_{	au_s^h})\cdot
abla_y p_\alpha(t-s,y-X_{	au_s^h})-b(s,X_{	au_s^h}^h)\cdot
abla_y p_\alpha(t-s,y-X_{	au_s^h}^h)]ds, with kernel time t-s and range [h,	au_t^h-h]. The gathering display instead asserts the remainder \int_h^t\E[\ldots
abla_y p_\alpha(t-	au_s^h,\ldots)]ds, with kernel time t-	au_s^h and range [h,t]. The two expressions do not coincide: replacing the kernel time produces an extra \Delta_{42}-type time-sensitivity term of order (s-	au_s^h)(t-s)^{-1-1/\alpha}, and extending the range adds the interval [	au_t^h-h,t]; neither difference is estimated anywhere in the paper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep \Delta_3 as defined in \eqref{DECOUP_ERR}; expanding through the densities gives |\Delta_3|\le C\bar p_\alpha(t,y-x)\int_h^{\tau_t^h-h}f(\tau_s^h)(t-s)^{-1/\alpha}ds, and the discrete Volterra-Grönwall lemma with kernel (t-s)^{-1/\alpha} yields f(t)\lesssim h^{\gamma/\alpha}(1+t^{-\beta/\alpha}) exactly as claimed. (Equivalently, derive the written remainder and estimate the additional kernel-difference terms via the cancellation of Lemma THE_LEMMA_FOR_THM.)
issues.overall_effect: The inequality that initiates the Grönwall-Volterra recursion for f(t)=\sup_{x,z}|\Gamma^h-\Gamma|/\bar p_\alpha is not a consequence of the stated decomposition as written, so the final step of Theorem thm-main's proof is unsupported.
issues.title: Grönwall remainder term does not match \Delta_3 produced by the decomposition
issues.why_classification: The correction is to carry the actual \Delta_3 into the Grönwall step, for which the same discrete Volterra argument applies verbatim; the theorem's conclusion, rate, and scope are unchanged.
